entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned Counsel for the applicant and Sri Yogendra Kumar, learned brief holder for the State.

2. The instant bail application, under Section 439 Cr.P.C., has been filed with a prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 432 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 352, 506 I.P.C., Police Station- Bansdeeh, District-Ballia, during pendency of the trial.
3. Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case.
The applicant is the mother-in-law of the informant.
The owner of the disputed property was the husband of the applicant.
By a registered deed dated 15.06.2022 he sold the property in favour of the applicant.
Thereafter, the said property was sold by the applicant to another person.

sentences.text: property was purchased by the husband of the applicant by his own means, the same was not the ancestral property.
A civil suit is pending between the parties before the competent court.
The dispute is primarily of civil in nature and has been given colour of a criminal case to harass the applicant.
At this stage, there is no cogent evidence to link the applicant with the offence.
The applicant is a lady and is in jail since 17.10.2023 having no criminal history and in case he is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the said liberty.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid submissions from the record.
5. Having heard counsel for the parties and having perused the record, this Court prima facie finds that the dispute is primarily of civil in nature.
A civil suit is pending between the parties before the competent court.
At this stage, there is no substantive evidence against the applicant.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.

The applicant is a lady and has remained confined for almost two months and after submission of the charge-sheet there is no hope of early conclusion of trial, more so when no reasonable apprehension has been brought to the fore by the State that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, would either tamper with the evidence or delay the trial or intimidate the witness,
without commenting on the merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.

6. Let the applicant, Smt. Chankali Devi, involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned on the following conditions that:
i. the applicant shall not temper with the prosecution evidence; ii. the applicant shall not pressurize the prosecution witness;and, iii. the applicant shall appear on each and every date fixed by the trial court.
7. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
